cases.title: A new pipe that ends on pit P8 joins it: the flow line says Open end -> P8
cases.plan_item: UX-PIPE-02 (daily case D03), the pipe-ends-on-a-pit half
cases.expected: After the setup (pit P8 at 150000,-80000 and a pipe leaving it), CD from the open point 130000,-80000 to the pit centre 150000,-80000 with levels 18.100 / 17.900 (a 0.2 m fall over 20 m is the default 1 IN 100; other levels open a "Grade mismatch" question that waits for an answer) prints 'Inserted flow arrow. Flow: Open end -> P8' once, makes exactly one new pipe object, and the pipe box sits at y -80112.5 like the pipe that leaves the pit. A twin that ends the pipe 2 m short of the pit (R02b_BROKEN) must not say 'Flow: Open end -> P8'.
cases.why_not_unit: The join is made by the live CD point landing against the real pit in the drawing.
not_automated: This case counts for 'a pipe ended on a pit joins it' only. The Pit Schedule row of P8 is read in R02 (the pipe that starts on the pit). The pipe's last vertex is not read: only CE's own command line and the pipe box row are checked.
cases.setup_note: shared setup SETUP-P8v run here for the first time at 07:50:01

cases.title: After PIT and CD the current layer is still BLOCKS, nothing new is on layer 0 or on BLOCKS, the pit is on STORMWATER PIT and the flow arrow on ARROW
cases.plan_item: UX-LYR-01 installed part (daily card D24); the never-recolour half is not built
cases.expected: After SETUP-P8 (PIT at 150000,-80000 and a CD pipe to 170000,-80000) the current layer CLAYER still reads BLOCKS (its value when the drawing opened); none of the new objects is on layer 0 or on BLOCKS; the one new pit block is on STORMWATER PIT; the one new flow arrow (TIM_CVL_ARROW) is on ARROW. The layers of the IL texts, the pipe label and the pipe object are recorded.
cases.why_not_unit: Layer choice and the current-layer restore happen in the live drawing's layer table during real PIT and CD runs.
not_automated: 'An existing layer is never recoloured' is NOT BUILT; the layer table colours are not read.
The pit label layer is covered by N05 (this setup escapes the label prompt, so no label exists here).
